newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd leader asks Turkey to help aid groups.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd leader asks Turkey to help aid groups.

text.p: Iraqi Kurd leader Jalal Talabani said on Friday he had asked Turkey to relax restrictions on Western aid groups entering northern Iraq for humanitarian operations.
"We have asked support...for NGO's to come through Turkey to Iraqi Kurdistan for humanitarian assistance to the Kurdish people," Talabani told a news conference.
Non-governmental organisations have criticised Turkey for blocking the movement of aid workers into the region and thus undermining their work.
Ankara says tighter restrictions are necessary to prevent Turkish Kurd rebels benefiting from humanitarian activities.
Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels use bases in northern Iraq, outside Baghdad's control since 1991, as part of their 12-year-old guerrilla war for self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
More than 21,000 people have died in the conflict. Large numbers of Turkish troops have crossed into Iraq on several occasions in pursuit of the guerrillas.

Talabani, leader of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), was visiting Turkey after two days of peace talks there between the PUK and its rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), which between them control northern Iraq.

The rival groups agreed to a U.S.-mediated ceasefire last October following months of clashes which escalated in August after the KDP joined with Iraqi troops to take control of the key Kurdish city of Arbil from Talabani's fighters.
The clashes gave Baghdad a foothold in Western-protected northern Iraq for the first time since the end of the 1991 Gulf War and weakened humanitarian operations there.

In December the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said it was phasing out operations at a refugee camp in the region because its work was blocked by "activists". Turkey says the Atrush camp was used as a base by the PKK.
